<laravel-boost-guidelines>
Laravel Boost guidelines curated by Laravel maintainers. This is a Laravel application using these versions: laravel/framework (LARAVEL) v12; laravel/prompts (PROMPTS) v0; laravel/mcp (MCP) v0; laravel/pint (PINT) v1; laravel/sail (SAIL) v1; phpunit/phpunit (PHPUNIT) v11. Follow app code conventions; when creating/editing a file, check sibling files for correct structure/approach/naming. Use descriptive names (e.g. `isRegisteredForDiscounts`). Reuse existing components before writing new ones. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover functionality and prove it works; prefer Unit/Feature tests. Stick to existing directory structure; don't create new base folders without approval. Do not change application's dependencies without approval. If no frontend change appears in UI, it could mean they need to run `bun run build`, `bun run dev`, or `composer run dev`. Ask them. Be concise in explanations. You must follow all existing code conventions used in this application. You are an expert with them all. Ensure you abide by these specific packages & versions.
This application uses Boost (MCP server with powerful tools). Use the `list-artisan-commands` tool when you need to call an Artisan command to double check available parameters. Whenever you share a project URL with the user you should use the `get-absolute-url` tool. Use the `tinker` tool when you need to execute PHP to debug code or query Eloquent models directly. Use `database-query` only to read from the database. Use `browser-logs` to read browser logs/errors/exceptions (only recent). Use `search-docs` before any other approaches for Laravel-ecosystem/version-specific docs. Pass multiple broad simple topic queries first (e.g. `['rate limiting', 'routing rate limiting', 'routing']`). Do not add package names to queries. You can pass multiple queries at once; most relevant results first. Use example query patterns (auto-stemming; AND logic; quoted phrases; mixed queries; multiple queries). Search the documentation before making code changes. Always use curly braces for control structures. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion in `__construct()`, e.g. `public function __construct(public GitHub $github) { }`. Do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters. Always use explicit return type declarations. Use appropriate PHP type hints. Prefer PHPDoc blocks over comments; never use comments within the code itself unless very complex. Add useful array shape type definitions when appropriate. Typically enum keys are TitleCase (e.g. `FavoritePerson`, `BestLake`, `Monthly`).

=== laravel/core rules ===
Use `php artisan make:` commands to create new files (migrations/controllers/models/etc.); list commands via `list-artisan-commands`. Pass `--no-interaction` to all Artisan commands; pass correct `--options`. If creating a generic PHP class, use `php artisan make:class`. Always use proper Eloquent relationship methods with return type hints; prefer relationships over raw joins. Use Eloquent models/relationships before suggesting raw DB queries; avoid `DB::`; prefer `Model::query()`. Prevent N+1 via eager loading; use query builder for very complex DB ops. When creating new models, create useful factories and seeders; ask if they need other things using `list-artisan-commands` to check options to `php artisan make:model`. For APIs, default to Eloquent API Resources and API versioning unless existing conventions differ. Always create Form Request classes for validation rather than inline validation in controllers; include both validation rules and custom error messages; check sibling Form Requests for array vs string validation rules. Use queued jobs for time-consuming operations with `ShouldQueue`. Use built-in auth/authorization (gates/policies/Sanctum/etc.). Generate links using named routes and `route()`. Do not use `env()` outside config files; use environment variables only in configuration files; use `config('app.name')` not `env('APP_NAME')`. For test models, use factories (check custom states). Faker: use `$this->faker->...` or `fake()` per existing conventions. Tests: use `php artisan make:test [options] {name}`; pass `--unit` for unit tests; most should be feature tests. If hit `Illuminate\Foundation\ViteException: Unable to locate file in Vite manifest`, run `bun run build` or ask to run `bun run dev` or `composer run dev`. Use `search-docs` for version specific documentation. Since Laravel 11, streamlined file structure: this project uses it. No middleware files in `app/Http/Middleware/`. `bootstrap/app.php` registers middleware/exceptions/routing files. `bootstrap/providers.php` has application specific service providers. **No app\Console\Kernel.php** - use `bootstrap/app.php` or `routes/console.php` for console configuration. **Commands auto-register**: files in `app/Console/Commands/` are automatically available. When modifying a column, migration must include all previously defined attributes for that column (otherwise dropped). Laravel 11 supports limiting eagerly loaded records natively: `$query->latest()->limit(10);`. Set casts in `casts()` method on models rather than `$casts` property, following existing conventions.

=== pint/core rules ===
You must run `vendor/bin/pint --dirty` before finalizing changes. Do not run `vendor/bin/pint --test`, simply run `vendor/bin/pint` to fix formatting issues.

=== phpunit/core rules ===
Tests use PHPUnit classes. Use `php artisan make:test --phpunit {name}`. If you see a test using "Pest", convert it to PHPUnit. Every time a test has been updated, run that singular test.
